title: Police curfew imposed around Mahara Prison
byline: A police curfew has been imposed with immediate effect until further notice across three Grama Niladhari divisions surrounding the Mahara Prison within the Ragama Police division to maintain peace and order.

title: Mahara Prison unrest brought under control; Curfew remains in force
byline: The unrest at Mahara Prison has been brought under control, with all inmates now confined to their cells, Police said.

title: Trump says he is cancelling strikes on Iran subject to ’rapidly’ making deal
byline: Donald Trump says he has cancelled strikes against Iran provided a deal was struck ’’rapidly’’ with the country.

title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13
byline: A small plane carrying tourists has crashed in Peru, killing all 13 people on board, according to local news reports and Peruvian officials.

title: Sri Lanka Women seal T20I series with six-wicket win over Pakistan
byline: Sri Lanka Women clinched the three-match T20 International series against Pakistan Women with a match to spare after registering a convincing six-wicket victory in the second T20I at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium on Sunday.

title: Five dead, 41 missing, after Indonesia ferry catches fire
byline: Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry carrying 271 people caught fire while at sea, officials say.

title: Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of Sri Lanka Tests
byline: asprit Bumrah is set to miss the two Test series against Sri Lanka, starting in Galle on August 15. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that the seamer continues to feel discomfort in his left knee after an initial assessment at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE). The stakeholders have decided that it’s not safe to push him back into cricket and advised a full recovery.

title: Government discusses Mullaitivu land issues at civil-military meeting
byline: Deputy Minister of Defence Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd.) chaired a high-level Civil-Military Coordination Meeting at the Mullaitivu Divisional Secretariat to discuss long-standing land issues and regional development in the Northern Province.

title: South Korea experiences its hottest day in modern history
byline: South Korea on Sunday saw its hottest day in modern history, with temperatures soaring to 42.5C (108.5F), the state weather agency said.

title: Mahara Prison begins transferring inmates after violent unrest
byline: The Department of Prisons said a number of inmates from Mahara Prison are being transferred to other prisons following the unrest that erupted at the facility yesterday (01).

title: Mahara Prison unrest damages multiple facilities
byline: The violent disturbance that erupted at Mahara Prison on Saturday (01) caused extensive damage to several prison facilities, including the rehabilitation division, visitors’ area, prison hospital, kitchen, industrial section, and a number of prison buildings, according to the Department of Prisons.

title: Sajith wants task force appointed to face El-Nino phenomenon
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa today called for the setting up of a task force to face the impending El-Nino phenomenon.

title: Fires on more than 250,000 acres of Washington state prompt evacuations
byline: Wildfires across more than a quarter of a million acres in Washington state have prompted widespread evacuations and power outages in the Spokane area, state officials said on Saturday ​evening.

title: Namal accuses government for Mahara prison unrest
byline: Claiming that the unrest at the Mahara prison is no longer an isolated incident, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa urged the government to stop firefighting and start fixing a prison system that is showing clear signs of institutional failure.

title: World breastfeeding week begins
byline: World Breastfeeding Week began yesterday (1) and will continue until August 7, with health authorities launching a nationwide campaign to raise awareness about the importance of breastfeeding.

title: Police curfew lifted in three Ragama GN divisions
byline: Measures have been taken to lift the police curfew that was imposed across three Grama Niladhari (GN) divisions in the Ragama area.

title: ISS astronauts grow kale and mustard sprouts to support future space missions
byline: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station (ISS) have successfully grown sprouts of Red Russian kale and Wasabi mustard greens as part of research aimed at developing sustainable food production for future space missions.

title: Police seize 292 kg of ganja headed for Sri Lanka, arrest three
byline: The Q Branch police seized 292 kg of ganja that was being taken for smuggling to Sri Lanka near Ramanathapuram and arrested three persons.

title: WestJet flight attendants go on strike after talks fall through, grounding flights
byline: Flight attendants at Canada’s WestJet went on strike on Sunday ‌after failing to reach a deal with the country’s second-largest carrier, grounding flights during the busy summer travel season.

title: AG clears draft bill to extend judges’ retirement age
byline: The Attorney General has granted legal clearance for the draft bill seeking to extend the retirement age of judges by two years, paving the way for the legislation to move to the next stage.

title: Mahara Prison situation brought under control; 104 inmates transferred
byline: The unrest that erupted inside the Mahara Prison on Saturday afternoon has been brought under control through a joint operation involving prison officials, the Sri Lanka Police, the Police Special Task Force (STF) and the Tri-Forces, the Department of Prisons said.

title: Five dead, 41 missing, after Indonesia ferry catches fire
byline: Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry carrying 271 people caught fire while at sea, officials say.

title: Helicopters fighting Greece wildfires collide in mid-air
byline: Two helicopters have collided in Greece as they were battling to control wildfires.

title: ‘There is no agreement’: Iran rejects Trump claim of Strait of Hormuz reopening deal
byline: Iran on Sunday denied reports that it had agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, rejecting US President Donald Trump’s claim that an outline of a deal with Tehran included the “immediate, complete, and total” reopening of the strategic waterway.

title: Minister suspects outside influence in Mahara Prison unrest
byline: Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara said that the unrest at Mahara Prison is fundamentally different from the incident reported at Negombo Prison, noting that the nature of the two incidents is not the same.

title: ISS astronauts grow kale and mustard sprouts to support future space missions
byline: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station (ISS) have successfully grown sprouts of Red Russian kale and Wasabi mustard greens as part of research aimed at developing sustainable food production for future space missions.
